tts_summary:
Good morning. This edition is focused entirely on company-specific pre-market news for Tuesday September 22nd — there's no broad macro or Fed commentary included today, so let's go straight to the movers.

The biggest story is Viking Therapeutics, which is surging pre-market after reporting positive trial results for its GLP-1 weight loss drug VK2735 — participants saw 22% weight loss. That's a strong data readout and a meaningful validation for Viking in the increasingly competitive obesity drug space. Watch for sympathy moves across the GLP-1 complex at the open.

On the earnings front, AutoZone technically beat on fiscal fourth quarter EPS — $56.05 versus the Street at $54.03 — but the quality of that beat is questionable. The upside was almost entirely driven by tariff refunds, which were a 145 basis point tailwind to gross margins, plus a non-cash LIFO adjustment worth another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture looks less impressive. Domestic comps came in at plus 1.6% against an expectation of plus 3.1% — a meaningful miss — and the operating expense ratio worsened by 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did note improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and expressed optimism about fiscal 2027, but this is not a clean beat.

MillerKnoll is a better earnings story. The office furniture and design company posted fiscal first quarter EPS of 53 cents versus consensus at 36 cents. Importantly, even backing out the 11 cent tariff refund benefit, clean EPS was 42 cents — still a solid beat. Sales missed at $923 million versus $943 million expected, but orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed modestly, EPS guidance was unchanged, and the second quarter EPS midpoint is in line with the Street. Net net, this reads as a genuine operational beat.

Cognex announced a roughly $500 million acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and physical AI applications. RealSense is growing revenues over 50% year-over-year and is expected to generate $80 to $90 million in sales. This is a strategic bet on the physical AI and robotics buildout — a high-conviction growth area.

THOR Industries missed on fiscal fourth quarter EPS — 78 cents versus 87 cents expected — with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%. Management's tone was cautious, blaming stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation for keeping the recreational vehicle retail environment soft. There are some green shoots — dealer inventory is lean and healthy, and the North American towable RV order backlog surged about 75% year-over-year — but formal fiscal 2027 guidance won't come until later this fall. A mixed print leaning negative.

Finally, Pentair named a new CFO effective November 1st — a routine transition, no financial impact.

Bottom line for today: Viking is the standout momentum name. MillerKnoll is the clean earnings beat. AutoZone and THOR are both complicated stories that could see selling pressure as the market digests the details. Stay focused.
